entries.grounds: OCR_CHECKS['declared'][1] (run.py:158-166) is the operator 'what to do' help for the declared check. The mutant empties the whole opening sentence, so declared[1] begins "v1.12.12 (182898c); what it did instead is the observed value above (another release or commit, ...). Run `<exe> version` yourself. ...". The removed clause is the ONLY place that states the diagnosis of a declared-check failure: the bytes matched the pin (so it is NOT a pin problem) but the binary's `version` line did not name the pinned release. After mutation the help opens mid-thought with a bare version number and the surviving 'the observed value above' is left with a dangling referent. Operator-read via ident['operator']=OCR_CHECKS[check][1] (run.py:215); ocr_refusal embeds it (run.py:224); on a REFUSED status it is raised as RunRefused (run.py:517) and printed 'aisef run: refused: <it>' exit 2 (cli.py:99); persisted as rec['ocr_identity']['operator'] in RUN.json (run.py:515, written sort_keys at run.py:675); and printed by `aisef run --check` as ready['ocr_identity'] (cli.py:90-94). All carry it verbatim; none parses it. An operator depends on it to tell a declared failure (do not re-pin; investigate the version declaration) from a pinned failure (re-hash/re-pin). The designated pinner test_each_check_says_what_it_is_and_what_the_operator_does exists to pin 'the words an operator reads in a refusal' (test_v21_ocr_identity.py:168) yet its declared do-list (:180-182) asserts review.ocr.sha256, v1.12.12, 182898c, '`<exe> version` yourself', 'review.finder to "model"', 'pin the sha256 of a build of Open Code Review v1.12.12 (182898c)', 'give it a new --out', 'run again' -- each of which ALSO occurs after the deleted sentence, so none fails; test_the_declared_operator_text_is_true_of_every_way_the_check_fails (:186-191) asserts DECLARED_WAYS.values(), all in the surviving '(another release or commit, ...)' clause. grep shows 'did not print the version line' / 'The file's bytes are the ones review.ocr.sha256 pins' occur only at run.py:159. entries.grounds: evidence_manifest (run.py:425-434) builds `files` as a list ending with the probe-observations glob; the mutant makes ONLY that last glob list(...) instead of sorted(...), so probe-observations entries are inserted into the returned {path: sha} dict in filesystem-glob order instead of name order (the four earlier globs stay sorted). The dict's key set and values are unchanged; only the insertion order of the probe-observations keys can differ, and only where the glob returns them out of name order. Every reader treats the result as a mapping: anchor_of (run.py:447) and the on-disk manifest write (run.py:677) both json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True) -- order-independent; verify.py:123/129 and bundle_cli.py:814/824 compare by dict == and by anchor -- order-independent; verify.py:130-131 / bundle_cli.py:825 sort the diff. The only order-asserting test, test_every_group_is_listed_in_name_order (test_v21_r3_detail_artifact.py:359-372), checks the groups sessions/, run/journals/, preflight/, review-findings/ -- NEVER probe-observations/; T14a (test_v21_kills3_T14a.py:144,190) names [..17..] but asserts by dict == with no probe-observations members; pm8_diagnostics_run.py:233-234 reads manifest[f'{DIR}/{name}'] by key and compares anchors. The function docstring (run.py:360-362 in the test, i.e. the manifest contract) states 'The manifest is a mapping and nothing reads its order'. Not EQUIVALENT: a direct caller's list(evidence_manifest(out)['files']) exposes the order (demonstrated: two mappings equal under == and under anchor_of/sort_keys differ under list()); AUDITED: no consumer, contract, document, test or operator the entry names depends on probe-observations order. RAN all 12 registered kill files on the mutant: 11 PASS; tests.v2.test_v21_identity errored=7 at BOTH baseline and mutant for a missing closure-evidence/v2/release/LEDGERLOCK-PROJECT.json (excluded by the prescribed archive paths) -- mutation-independent; after adding that file via `git show 4ec961e...:...LEDGERLOCK-PROJECT.json`, test_v21_identity PASSES at baseline and on the mutant. No kill file fails on the mutant while passing unmutated -> SURVIVED. Matches docs/v2.1/decisions/B03-R3-detail.md:185 (these sorted()->list() manifest mutants are FS-order-dependent survivors).
